lines: Si neſcis, oculi ſunt in amore duces.
Et voila pourquoy Iuuenal eſtime vne choſe prodigi-
euſe & trop eſtrange, qu'vn Aueugle ſoit amoureux. Et
Martial ſe mocque de Codrus, lequel priué de la veuë,
neantmoins depuis deuint extremement paſſiõné pour
l'amour d'vne femme.
Plus credit nemo, quam tota Codrus in vrbe,
Cùm ſit tam pauper, quomodo! cæcus amat. {c}
Et à laquelle ledit du Tilh auoit don
né pluſieurs priuées & particulieres en-
ſeignes. Meſmes des actes & propos qui
interuiennent le plus ſecrettement en-
tre mariez, & qu'autres ne peuuent bon
nemẽt ſçauoir, ou entẽdre: Iuſques à luy
enſeigner les lieux, temps, & heures des
actes ſecrets de mariage (plus aiſez beau
coup à comprendre, qu'honneſte à reci-
ter, ou eſcrire) & les propos qu'auant, a-
pres, & en l'acte, ils auroyent tenuz. S'e-
ſtoit auſsi perſuadée auec les autres, que
ledit du Tilh eſtoit certainement Mar-
tin Guerre ſon mari.
La femme de Q. Sertorius à Rome, & Ieanne fille
du comte Balduin de Flandres, furẽt vn peu mieux aui-
ſées: car quand celuy qui ſe diſoit fils de Q., Sertorius,
& de pluſieurs ſuiuy comme tel à Rome, vn iour ſe pre
ſenta à la femme de Sertorius cõme à ſa mere, luy don-
nãt des enſeignes fort familieres, & neãtmoins ſecrettes
& veritables: elle d'vne grande pertinacité, & vertueuſe
Properce an
liure ij. des ele
gies.

margin_notes.beside_line: Cùm ſit tam pauper, quomodo! cæcus amat. {c}

uncertain.text: Si neſcis, oculi ſunt in amore duces.
uncertain.note: continues_prev set true: this is the pentameter completing a Propertius couplet whose hexameter must stand at the foot of p020; p020 is not yet transcribed, so the judgement is from sense alone.

No marker b is visible anywhere in the body of this page, although the note with key b is printed in the margin beside the second body line. The marker b presumably stands at the end of the Propertius quotation on p020. Recorded here as a note without a body marker.

Second word transcribed as printed: the glyph after 'a' has its two stems joined at the TOP (arch), unlike the clear italic 'u' of 'liure' on the next line, where they join at the bottom. Read as 'an'; the sense wants 'au liure ij.' and finals elsewhere have 'au liure', so this is probably a turned u. Reader B may well read 'au'.
Same word as in note b and heavily inked here; the second letter is a blot in which the top join is the likeliest reading. Transcribed 'an' for consistency with note b; 'au' is a live alternative.

uncertain.text: Cùm ſit tam pauper, quomodo! cæcus amat. {c}
uncertain.note: 'quomodo!' — the mark is a vertical stroke over a point, i.e. an exclamation, not the question mark the received text of Martial III.15 has. Transcribed as printed (sic); could conceivably be a damaged '?'.

uncertain.text: ſées: car quand celuy qui ſe diſoit fils de Q., Sertorius,
uncertain.note: After 'Q' the print sets a point and then a comma ('Q.,Sertorius,'), both clearly inked; normalized for spacing to 'Q., Sertorius,'. The comma looks like a compositor's slip; transcribed as printed. Line 1 of the same paragraph has plain 'Q. Sertorius'.

uncertain.text: nemẽt ſçauoir, ou entẽdre: Iuſques à luy
uncertain.note: The marks over the e of 'nemẽt' and 'entẽdre' are flat bars (tildes for omitted n), distinguishable from the sloped acute of 'paſſiõné'/'priuées' elsewhere on the page; transcribed ẽ.
